skill.name: python-venv-manager
skill.description: Manage Python virtual environments, dependencies, project setup, and troubleshooting workflows.
skill.summary: Guides reproducible Python environments from venv basics to Poetry, pyenv, and Docker workflows.
skill.author: CuriousLearner

security_audit.summary: The skill is mostly Python environment setup documentation, not executable malware. Confirmed risks are unsafe remote installer pipelines, shell expansion from dependency files, and examples that write .env files with sensitive placeholders; many other static matches are Markdown fences or safe configuration examples. No prompt-injection text was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Remote installer commands execute fetched code directly.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell and curl-to-Python snippets with package-manager installs, checksum verification, or explicit download and review steps.

remediation.issue: Dependency migration examples expand file content into install commands.
remediation.suggestion: Parse requirements with a Python packaging parser and pass validated package names as explicit arguments.

remediation.issue: Examples create .env files containing secret and database placeholders.
remediation.suggestion: Use .env.example for non-secret defaults, mark all values as placeholders, and remind users to keep real secrets out of version control.

remediation.issue: Shell initialization examples rely on eval output from pyenv.
remediation.suggestion: Explain that users should review shell initialization output and only apply it from a trusted pyenv installation.

content.value_statement: Python projects often break when environments and dependencies drift. This skill gives repeatable setup, migration, and troubleshooting workflows for isolated Python development.
actual_capabilities: Compares venv, virtualenv, Poetry, Pipenv, pyenv, and pip-tools workflows.
Provides steps to create, activate, rebuild, and remove Python virtual environments.
Guides requirements files, dependency groups, lock files, and dependency export workflows.
Helps migrate existing requirements or Pipenv projects to Poetry.
Includes setup examples for pytest, linting, pre-commit, Docker, and project layout.
Troubleshoots import errors, dependency conflicts, SSL problems, and permission issues.
limitations: It provides guidance and command templates, not automatic validation of every local environment.
Some installation examples execute external tools and require user review before running.
It does not replace dependency source review or supply chain security checks.
Version numbers in examples may need updates for current project policies.

use_cases.title: Start a new Python project
use_cases.description: Create an isolated environment, choose a dependency manager, and set up tests and formatting.

use_cases.title: Migrate dependency tooling
use_cases.description: Move from manual requirements files or Pipenv to Poetry while preserving reproducible installs.

use_cases.title: Standardize team onboarding
use_cases.description: Document repeatable setup steps for Python versions, virtual environments, Docker, and quality tools.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic environment
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a small project
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up a new Python virtual environment for this project. Use built-in venv, create a requirements file, and list activation steps for macOS, Linux, and Windows.

prompt_templates.title: Fix dependency errors
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this Python import or dependency conflict. Check the active interpreter, installed packages, dependency tree, and steps to rebuild the environment safely.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate to Poetry
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a migration from requirements files to Poetry. Separate runtime and development dependencies, preserve pinned versions, and describe verification steps before removing old files.

prompt_templates.title: Design a reproducible workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reproducible Python setup for a team project. Include Python version management, dependency locking, Docker integration, testing tools, and supply chain safety checks.

output_examples.input: I need a clean Python environment for a small command line project.
output: Recommendation to use built-in venv for a simple project.
A setup checklist covering activation, package installation, test tools, and dependency capture.
Notes on keeping the environment directory out of version control.

output_examples.input: This project has requirements files and I want to move to Poetry.
output: A migration plan with backup, dependency grouping, lock file generation, and verification steps.
Warnings to review dependency sources before installing converted packages.

output_examples.input: My tests fail because Python imports the wrong package version.
output: A diagnostic sequence for interpreter path, active environment, installed versions, and dependency conflicts.
A safe rebuild path that avoids global package changes.

best_practices: Use one isolated environment per project and document the required Python version.
Pin production dependencies and review lock files before release.
Keep secrets out of version control and use example files for non-secret defaults.
anti_patterns: Installing project dependencies into the global Python environment.
Running remote installer scripts without checking their source and integrity.
Committing virtual environment directories, lock file conflicts, or real secret values.

faq.question: Does this skill create environments automatically?
faq.answer: It provides commands and guidance. Execution depends on the agent tools and user approval.

faq.question: Which dependency manager does it recommend?
faq.answer: It compares several tools and often recommends Poetry or pip-tools for reproducible projects.

faq.question: Can it help with multiple Python versions?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes pyenv workflows for project-specific Python versions and virtual environments.

faq.question: Does it support Docker workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Docker examples for virtual environments and Poetry-based builds.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use local environment variables or ignored configuration files, and never commit real secret values.

faq.question: Is it safe to run every command as written?
faq.answer: No. Review installer, shell, and dependency commands before execution, especially commands that fetch remote code.
